findings: Both sequences reframe the athlete and barbell substantially between standing setup, bent setup, transition and lockout. Frame 1 has a much larger head, shoes and plates than frame 0, despite the same viewpoint; the feet also shift vertically. These changes exceed expected joint motion and cause visible size/anchor jumps during animation.

Chain routing changes between phases: the transition has single hanging lengths on the image-right side, while lockout shows long closed hanging loops on both sides. This is an equipment continuity concern beyond ordinary lifting of slack chain.

Rack uprights change lean, spacing and exposed height across frames, with corresponding bench/support shifts. Female frames 1 and 2 have tall uprights that shorten markedly in frame 3; male uprights also change height/position between 1 and 2. These stationary geometry changes cannot be explained by bar travel and will visibly morph during animation.
Black wrist wraps appear on both wrists only in male frame 2; other male frames show bare wrists.
A pointed dark extension beneath the foreground shoe is visible against the light background in all female frames; it reads as an extra sole/shadow fragment rather than the rounded shoe sole.

Opaque white wedges remain in enclosed background gaps between bent legs, roller supports and bench in all eight frames; additional white gaps appear beside the neck/inside bent arms. They stay white on the dark preview instead of revealing the background.

Stationary bench and roller assembly change size and position across both sequences. Frame 0 is noticeably larger than later frames; the bench left end and support base shift between action phases. These equipment changes are independent of the intended torso curl and would create animation wobble.

The stationary bench changes construction, support layout and viewing angle across the sequence. Frames 1–2 use a much steeper image diagonal than 0 and 3; head/bench anchors and leg positioning shift substantially. These changes exceed the expected arm movement of a fly and would make the animation jump.

Bench perspective, support construction and head/foot anchors change substantially between frames. The athlete also switches from shorts with bare lower legs in 0/3 to full-length leggings in 1/2. These are obvious stationary-equipment and clothing discontinuities.
Pale gray opaque residue forms a narrow ground-shaped strip around the front bench foot and beneath the long base rail/right foot, conspicuous on the dark background.

Stationary bench structure, angle and placement change substantially between frames in both sequences. Male frame 0 has a curved brace and different foot/base geometry; later frames switch among straight supports and different leg/roller positions. Female frames change support structure, pad segmentation and bench angle. Torso/head and anchored feet shift with this redrawing, beyond the expected elbow/bar movement, causing visible animation jumps.
Female frames 0–2 show plates on both ends of the EZ bar, while frame 3 shows a bare bar with both plates absent. This is an obvious load/equipment discontinuity during the same repetition.

Stationary decline bench changes geometry and placement across the sequence: frame 1 has a separate head pad and round floor feet, frame 2 introduces a diagonal support brace, and frames 0/3 use different support angles and foot shapes. The roller assembly and bench endpoints also shift. These equipment changes cannot be explained by the torso crunch and would visibly pop during animation.

Stationary bench changes substantially across the sequence: frame 0 has a steep diagonal support, frame 1 a flatter bench and displaced roller assembly, frame 2 a divided cushion, and frame 3 a nearly vertical telescoping support with a single continuous cushion. Floor anchors and bench angle shift beyond the athlete motion, producing obvious animation discontinuity.

Both ordered sequences move the step and hand-contact baseline vertically between frames, visibly lifting the whole ground plane during the lowered poses and dropping it on return. The step also shifts horizontally and changes apparent size, especially male frame 0 versus frames 1–3. These fixed support changes are separate from legitimate elbow and torso movement and would produce conspicuous animation bouncing.

Thin light fringe and scattered pale edge pixels remain around the athlete and step, most apparent against black at hair, back, arms and shoe contours. The illustration remains usable; no large interior checkerboard patches or incorrectly cut clothing holes are visible.

Bench geometry changes substantially across both sequences: feet switch between round crossbars and rectangular bases, support struts and handle mounts change design, and pad divisions, bench angle and floor anchors shift. These are changes to stationary equipment, beyond the intended leg and pelvic movement, and would produce obvious morphing/jumps during animation.
Male frames 0–2 have featureless facial interiors while frame 3 introduces detailed eyes, nose, mouth and facial shading. The abrupt rendering change is visible within the same sequence.

Stationary Smith rack and decline bench change perspective, geometry and anchor positions across both sequences. Male frame 0 is nearly frontal, frame 2 is much more side-on, and frames 1/3 show a steeper bench with different supports and foot placement. Female frame 3 shifts the right upright markedly inward and changes the bench/leg setup relative to frames 0–2. These changes exceed press motion and would visibly jump during animation.
Female frame 3 changes the predominantly black shoes in frames 0–2 to white shoes.

In the male sequence, frame 2 enlarges the athlete's head/body and barbell plates substantially relative to frames 0, 1 and 3, while the stationary platform and feet move upward. The plate diameter and body scale change cannot be explained by the deadlift motion. Platform shape and shoe details also vary between frames. This produces a conspicuous zoom/anchor jump during playback.

In the female sequence, frame 2 enlarges the athlete's head/body and barbell plates substantially relative to frames 0, 1 and 3, while the stationary platform and feet move upward. The plate diameter and body scale change cannot be explained by the deadlift motion. Platform shape and shoe details also vary between frames. This produces a conspicuous zoom/anchor jump during playback.
Thin light dotted fringes trace portions of athlete contours and the inner/outer box edges on dark backgrounds. No substantial opaque background or enclosed checkerboard is visible.

Both stationary boxes change size, spacing and placement across each sequence. For example, the male tall box moves from approximately x558..852 in frame 0 to x624..888 in frame 1 and x519..775 in frame 3; the female tall box similarly shifts left and changes proportions at frame 3. The ground baseline also shifts. These redraw changes make the equipment visibly jump during animation, beyond the athlete's intended leap.

The stationary dip stands change design, spacing and handle height across both sequences. Male frames 0–2 have long straight posts without visible bases, while frame 3 introduces shorter stands with triangular braces and feet. Female frame 0 has braced stands, frame 1 has flat bolted feet and different handle joints, and frames 2–3 return to long posts without bases. The substantial handle-height and athlete-scale changes make the animation jump; they are not explained by the athlete bending elbows or leaning forward.

The male sequence changes stationary dip-stand height, spacing, base position and construction across frames. Frame 0 is narrower with lower handles; frames 1 and 2 enlarge the athlete and raise/spread the handles while the head stays near the same canvas height. Frame 2 also changes the stand joints/base design, particularly the male stand losing the diagonal braces. Frame 3 changes the apparatus again. These changes exceed the athlete's legitimate dip movement and would cause obvious apparatus morphing and scale jumps in animation.

The female sequence changes stationary dip-stand height, spacing, base position and construction across frames. Frame 0 is narrower with lower handles; frames 1 and 2 enlarge the athlete and raise/spread the handles while the head stays near the same canvas height. Frame 2 also changes the stand joints/base design, particularly the male stand losing the diagonal braces. Frame 3 changes the apparatus again. These changes exceed the athlete's legitimate dip movement and would cause obvious apparatus morphing and scale jumps in animation.

The stationary bench changes from a short, narrow pad with closely overlapping upright supports in frame 0 to a broad bench in frames 1–2, then splayed legs in frame 3. The bench and foot block also shift horizontally and change size/perspective. These changes exceed heel-raise motion and would visibly jump in animation.

The stationary bench changes pad proportions, leg spacing and support geometry, especially the splayed legs in frame 2 versus upright legs in frames 0, 1 and 3. The foot block shifts substantially and changes width across the sequence. These changes are not explained by calf-raise motion.

Opaque white/light checkerboard remains inside kettlebell handle openings in every frame. Large enclosed white patches remain between torso and lowered arm in male 0, 2, 3 and female 0, 1, 2, 3; these stay white on the dark background.
Detached white/checkerboard blocks bridge the space between the shoes, especially conspicuous in female frame 3; male frames 1 and 2 also have scattered blocks and shoe-edge residue.
White residue extends below the shoe soles.

Large red muscle-highlight patches appear only in male frame 1, disappearing in 0, 2 and 3. Female frame 0 lacks the prominent red shoulder/thigh patches present in 1 through 3. This causes conspicuous visual flashing across each sequence.

Opaque white/light checkerboard remains in the enclosed gap between the lowered arm and torso/shorts/thigh in every frame. It is especially extensive in both frame 3 poses and plainly visible on the dark background.
Small white scraps extend beyond shoe soles, with thin pale perimeter fringe on portions of the athlete and equipment. Male frame 0 also has a tiny isolated speck below the feet.
Male frame 0 feet sit approximately 45-50 pixels higher than the bent frames on the 768-pixel canvas, causing a visible baseline jump. The changing overhead height itself is expected windmill motion.
Baked checkerboard in overhead arm gaps and between squatting legs
Detached ground and colored specks beneath jumping figures
Small pale background remnants near hair and shoes
Large opaque white/light-gray checkerboard fills the gap between the legs and extends around the shoes. Visible on both backgrounds and especially conspicuous on dark.
Opaque pale background remains in the enclosed gap between the image-right arm and torso.
Thin pale contour fringe and small exterior residue around the shoes are visible against dark backgrounds.
Top of hair touches and is cropped by the upper canvas boundary, unlike preceding frames with a small top margin.
Stationary feet shift modestly horizontally through each sequence, most visibly between phases 1 and 2; body height remains broadly consistent.
All eight frames have baked white/checkerboard background inside stands and white edge/floor remnants.
Both frame 2 images abruptly shorten the stationary stands and contain stray right-side fragments.
Frame 3 shifts the front stand and character relative to setup; female frame 3 is substantially larger.
Large opaque white/light-gray checkerboard patches remain between the legs from shorts to shoes. These remain visible against both backgrounds and flash on/off across the sequence.
White background remnants remain in the gap between the lowered arm and torso; widest in male 0/3 and female 0/3, narrower in male 1/2 and female 2.
Irregular pale ground remnants bridge or extend around the shoes, with a fine light fringe along portions of the outer silhouette on dark backgrounds.

White/light-gray checkerboard remains in the enclosed spaces beside the bench's right support and between the legs in all eight frames. It is conspicuous against dark backgrounds and is not part of the equipment.
A large opaque checkerboard panel fills the space between the raised arms in both full-extension frames.

Opaque white background remains between the legs in every frame; male and female frames 1 and 2 also contain large white gaps between raised arms. Female frames additionally retain white space between head/ponytail and bench. These remain white against the dark background.

Frames 2 and 3 have abrupt vertical cuts through the leftmost shoe/toe silhouette inside the canvas. Frame 2 of both genders also has a detached shoe-like fragment to the right of the bench. This is artwork clipping, not canvas-edge contact.
Male frame 1 has a small isolated dark speck left of the shoe; female frame 1 has a detached fragment to the right of the bench base.
Bench geometry and stationary foot locations shift between frames, most noticeably in frames 2 and 3, introducing a visible positional wobble beyond the intended arm motion.

Substantial opaque white islands fill the space between the legs in all eight frames, continuing into pale ground residue between/around the shoes. White islands also remain in the image-right arm/torso gaps in frames 0 and 3 of both variants (a smaller gap is visible in male frame 1). These stay white against the dark preview, rather than revealing the background.
Small white slivers remain at the outer ponytail in the female frames.

Both sequences translate horizontally: the head, torso and planted shoes move right in frame 1, back left in frame 2, and right again in frame 3 compared with frame 0. The displacement is modest but visible in stationary anchors, beyond the intended forearm curl movement. Overall height stays similar.
All eight frames contain opaque white background in enclosed body gaps and gray/white floor remnants adjoining pale shoe soles.
Female frame 1 has very tight top padding.

Opaque white background remains in the enclosed gaps between the bent legs and between the arms/dumbbells and torso. It is conspicuous on dark backgrounds, particularly the large panel between the extended arms in frame 2. Irregular pale gray/white ground residue also extends beneath the shoes, torso and head.

Frame 2 pulls the stationary feet and head inward and reduces body scale relative to frames 0/1/3 in both variants, most visibly in the male sequence. Small shifts in the resting head, feet and knees accompany other transitions. This is separate from the intended arm press motion.

Opaque white enclosed background remains between the legs and bench support in every frame, with ragged pale residue underneath bench feet and around shoes. Frames 0 and 3 of both genders additionally have a large opaque white region between raised arms; female frames also retain white at the neck/hair gap. These patches remain white against the dark diagnostic background.
The outer plate of the image-left dumbbell ends at a straight vertical cut inside the canvas, truncating its rounded silhouette. The rest of the movement remains recognizable.

Bench supports and planted shoes shift laterally between phases in both sequences, with modest changes in bench geometry and body framing. These stationary-anchor shifts are distinct from the intended arm opening and closing.
Large opaque white triangular background remains between the inclined bench, hanging arms and lower support. It is conspicuous on dark backgrounds and appears/disappears across the male sequence.

Small opaque white enclosed gaps remain between hanging forearms (frames 0 and 3) or under the bent near elbow (frame 2); white slivers also remain between the legs and bench. These do not follow the dark background.

Jagged pale ground/shadow remnants and small detached pale flecks remain around the shoes and bench base, conspicuous on the dark background. White circular bench openings also persist; whether these are intended hardware highlights is uncertain.

Large opaque white regions remain between raised arms and inside the triangular bench support in every frame. Female frames also retain white fill between the legs. Jagged pale residue extends around feet and beneath the bench, conspicuous on the dark background.

Frame 2 in both sets has a straight vertical cut through the image-left shoe and a flat cut across the tops of the dumbbells. Frame 3 has a straight vertical cut through the image-left knee/lower leg and shoe. These cuts occur within the transparent canvas, so additional outer padding does not recover the missing artwork.
A detached dark fragment appears to the right near foot height in frame 1; frame 2 has a larger detached shoe-like fragment in the same outer region, in both gender sets.

Both ordered sequences show the bench, hips, and planted feet translating left from frame 0 to frame 2 and shifting right again in frame 3, with apparent scale/framing changes. The stationary bench movement is distinct from the intended shoulder raise and will visibly jump in animation.

Opaque white strips remain between the arm and torso in every frame. Standing frames 0 and 2 also retain white fill between the calves. These areas stay white on the dark preview rather than revealing the background.
Pale exterior flecks/fringe remain around the shoe soles; lunge frames 1 and 3 have a conspicuous pale patch beneath the lowered knee and small detached residue toward the rear shoe.

Stationary bench changes geometry and vertical placement between frames in both sequences. Male frame 0 has splayed legs, frame 1 adds a long lower crossbar, and frames 2/3 remove it; bench height and floor anchors jump markedly. Female bench feet, braces and height also change across 0–3. These changes cannot be explained by forearm pronation and will visibly disrupt animation.

Male dumbbell changes from a single broad end plate in frame 0 to multiple stacked plates in frame 1, then back to a single broad plate in frames 2/3. This is a change in equipment construction beyond the intended rotation.

The stationary bench is redrawn with changing geometry and placement across both sequences. Male frame 0 has cylindrical base ends, while frames 1–3 use rectangular feet with changing support/base layouts. Female frame 0 has a long lower pad under the shins and a broad rectangular base; frames 1–3 lose that pad and use a substantially steeper, shorter bench with a different frame. The torso and feet also shift with this bench change, particularly female 0 to 1. These changes exceed the expected arm movement and would cause obvious animation discontinuity.

Male frame 1 has conspicuous mottled clothing texture unlike the smoother neighboring frames; female frame 2 also has more textured clothing. Faces, hair and general charcoal/red illustration language remain recognizable, but texture changes will flicker.

In both sequences frame 2 markedly reduces head-to-foot body size while fitting the overhead dumbbell into the canvas. Head and shoulders drop substantially and the body narrows despite straight standing legs. This is whole-body rescaling rather than the intended arm movement. Other frames also vary in foot baseline and body proportions.
A conspicuous flat gray patch extends outside and between the shoes, with jagged transparent breaks and isolated flecks below the body. It flashes into the sequence only in this frame.

Female frame 2 exposes a broad midriff while other frames have a full-length tank; frame 3 changes the center-part hairstyle to side-swept bangs. The shirt change may partly reflect arm elevation, but the overall appearance transition is noticeable.
Male dumbbell changes between hexagonal solid ends in frames 0/2 and round plate-style ends in frames 1/3.

In both variants, bent-arm frames 1 and 2 have visibly larger bodies than extended-arm frames 0 and 3 despite similar foot baselines. Head, torso and leg lengths change together; this is scale pumping rather than the intended elbow movement. Foot placement and body angle also shift, especially male frame 3. This materially disrupts a stationary standing extension animation.

Male frame 3 alone includes a flat opaque gray oval under and between the shoes. It is conspicuous on the dark background and appears/disappears within the sequence; it may be an authored ground shadow rather than accidental residue.

Opaque white/light patterned background remains in the enclosed gap between the working arm and torso in frames 0, 1 and 3 of both variants. These patches are conspicuous on the dark background and change shape through the sequence.
Thin pale intermittent fringe and small light edge specks surround portions of the silhouette, most apparent on the dark background around the head, limbs and shoes.

Bench frame, supports, feet, padding and angle change substantially between phases in both sequences; dumbbells switch between round and hexagonal heads. Stationary equipment and foot anchors visibly jump, beyond the intended elbow curl movement.

Male frames 0 and 2 have short dark hair, while 1 and 3 have bald oval mannequin-like heads. Frame 3 also changes the sleeveless top into a short-sleeved top and uses conspicuous joint/anatomy outlines. Identity and drawing treatment change visibly across the loop.

Broad pale ground strips beneath the bench contain visible baked checkerboard patterns, especially female frame 0; female frame 3 has a ragged pale strip. These remain conspicuous on the dark background.
Thin stray light marks remain at the extreme canvas edges, visible on the dark preview, separate from the athlete and bench.

Irregular opaque pale gray/white fragments remain beneath and between the shoes, with scattered pale edge fringe around the cutouts. Clearly visible on dark backgrounds; these are outside the footwear, not sole highlights.

Male frame 3 is noticeably smaller than frames 0–2 while the soles remain near the same baseline. Head, torso, limbs and dumbbells shrink together; this is not shoulder elevation from the shrug and creates a visible size jump on return.
Female return frame 3 has a modest reduction in overall height and slight lateral change relative to the earlier frames; the shoulder raise in frame 2 itself is appropriate exercise movement.

Broad irregular white/light-gray fragmented patches remain around the shoes and beneath the bench. These are highly conspicuous on dark backgrounds and vary between frames, materially harming the transparent cutout presentation.

Small skin-highlight areas appear dark against black and light against the light background, including forehead and knee highlights; these are unwanted transparent pinholes. Thin intermittent pale fringe is also visible around silhouettes and equipment.

The left end of the bench pad and horizontal metal rail terminate at a straight vertical cut inside the canvas; the left support leg is missing. The complete bench in earlier frames becomes visibly truncated in frame 3.
One circular opening in the bench rail contains an opaque white interior that stays white against the dark preview, unlike the adjacent transparent openings.

The stationary bench shifts horizontally between frames, particularly from 0 to 1 and back to 2 in both sequences. Its floor level is mostly stable; this horizontal shift is separate from the athlete's expected vertical step-up motion.
Detached extra fingers float to the right of the athlete's intact outstretched hand in both frame 1 images.
The image-left hand ends at a straight vertical cutoff inside the transparent canvas, with fingers missing. This is a baked artwork cutoff, not the canvas boundary.

Both standing sequences translate laterally as arms open and close: frame 1 feet and torso shift substantially left from frame 0, then return right in frame 2 and left in frame 3. Foot placement should remain anchored for this arm movement; body height and identity remain broadly consistent.
Large opaque white area fills the gap between the male setup legs, conspicuous against the dark background.
The right barbell plate stack is cut off by a straight vertical edge within the canvas in both setup frames; its outer side and bar end are absent.
An unrelated partial weight plate and bar end float to the left of the otherwise complete barbell in both frame-1 illustrations.
Small white wedges remain inside the bent-arm/bar/shoulder gaps instead of showing the dark background.
Thin pale fringe and scattered light pixels follow portions of the silhouette, plates and soles, most visible on dark backgrounds.

The front-foot support plate moves horizontally across successive frames although it serves as the stationary elevated support. The descent of the torso is expected exercise motion; the plate drift introduces limited animation jitter.

Stationary machine geometry changes substantially in both sequences. Male seats switch from angled support to box pedestal to broad solid base to four-leg stool; female seats switch from raised pedestal to floor block to stacked cushions to framed block. Towers, pulleys and footplates also change construction and position. These are equipment redesigns, not exercise movement, and materially disrupt animation.

Male frames 0 and 2 are shirtless with red muscle overlays, while 1 and 3 add a black tank top. Female frames alternate a longer top and cropped top with exposed lower back; red muscle rendering also changes. Clothing and presentation visibly switch within each animation.
Upper machine rails terminate at the top canvas edge in male 0/2 and female 0/1/3. Athlete and active handle remain visible; clipping is limited to tower tops.

Female sequence visibly changes the exercise ball's diameter and ground height: frame 2 has a larger ball than frame 3, while frame 3 raises both ball and shoes relative to frames 1 and 2. The stationary support and planted feet therefore shift together beyond the intended torso crunch motion, producing a noticeable scale/anchor discontinuity.

Male sequence has limited ball/foot anchor drift and ball-size variation, most apparent from frame 0 to frame 1 and frame 2 to frame 3. The torso motion remains readable and all artwork stays inside the canvas.

Both ordered sequences change athlete/equipment scale and hand placement. Male frame 2 has markedly larger arms, head and ball than frames 0/3; female frame 2 also enlarges the ball and moves the supporting hands down/right. Ball size contracts again in frame 3. These changes exceed the knee-tuck motion and would produce visible zoom/ground-contact jumps in animation.

Male frame 1 has a thin broken pale perimeter around hair, torso, hands and ball on the dark background. Female frames 1 and 3 show small pale jagged outlines around shoe edges. The limited residue does not obscure the poses.

Both sequences substantially reposition the torso, head, free arm and planted/bent-leg foot between straight-arm frames 0/3 and bent-arm frames 1/2. The head jumps upward and the bent-leg foot moves laterally; body angle and leg geometry also change. These changes exceed the pressing arm's genuine motion and produce a visibly discontinuous floor-press sequence.
Female frames 0/1 show a projecting ponytail, while 2/3 show a compact gathered/bun-like hairstyle. This visible hairstyle change adds identity discontinuity.

Female frame 2 changes from the left working arm to the right working arm and rotates the torso/stance; frame 3 immediately returns to the left arm. This produces an abrupt side/orientation jump in the ordered sequence rather than a continuous rotation/return. The README allows mirrored action, but this isolated opposite-side pose still needs sequence review.
The male shoulder muscle highlight is absent in frame 0, then appears with changing size/shape in frames 1–3; this creates a visible appearance pop.
Male shoe orientation and stance width vary across frames while overall body height remains similar. The modest foot/leg shifts can add jitter to a standing arm-rotation animation.

The working elbow moves substantially away from the torso and the arm becomes increasingly extended, especially male frame 3. The sequence reads as an outward arm reach rather than a clearly isolated bent-elbow external rotation. Exercise mechanics need manual review before acceptance.

Thin pale discontinuous outlines are visible around parts of the body, hair and band against the dark background. No broad opaque background, checkerboard interior or substantial unwanted holes observed.

The female band endpoint shifts horizontally across frames (furthest right in frames 1 and 2), despite appearing to represent a fixed anchor. Small body/foot placement changes are also visible; overall scale and identity remain consistent.

Broad opaque white/gray patches beneath the shoes and machine base, with ragged white residue around hair, limbs, cable and inside the machine. These are conspicuous on the dark background and appear abruptly after frame 0.
Thin pale outlines and scattered white flecks along figure, cable and machine edges, including interior machine rails; most visible on dark backgrounds.

Stationary machine shifts laterally and changes width slightly between frames, with smaller shifts in feet and ground shadow. Clothing texture also changes from speckled frame 0 to smoother later frames.
Clothing shading becomes conspicuously mottled in frame 3 compared with the smoother opening frames; figure and machine remain recognizable.
